batch: Classify eleven unclassified works from publisher, journal, and university repository abstracts
policy: These are work-scope judgments only. They do not certify complete object extraction, endorse readings, resolve identities, or change text and media rights.

entries.basis: Oxford University Press abstract for DOI 10.1093/jss/fgaa038 describes an analysis of bowl orthography as evidence for the Babylonian Hebrew vocalization tradition.

Cambridge University Press abstract for DOI 10.1017/S0041977X17000465 describes a philological re-examination of obscure bowl passages, lexemes and meanings; its preliminary edition of one bowl supports rather than displaces that linguistic purpose.
Ca' Foscari's repository abstract for DOI 10.1163/15700720-12341310 describes a study of Ephesians 6:10-17 on IBC 3 in relation to biblical citation and religious identification.
Ca' Foscari's repository abstract for DOI 10.1515/janeh-2020-0004 describes an analysis of Northern Mesopotamian demons and the historical fate of Hatrene inhabitants and cults.
The journal abstract for DOI 10.7817/jameroriesoci.138.4.0863 describes a cross-period comparison of double-bowl sets and double-jar burial practice.
University of Groningen abstract for DOI 10.1017/S0041977X19000363 describes a study of orality, textuality and performative utterances across bowl spells.
Brill abstract for DOI 10.1163/17455227-01301005 describes comparison of lost midrashim in the New Testament and Aramaic bowls.
University of Catania abstract for DOI 10.1163/17455227-01301007 describes a linguistic and cultural reconsideration of the Jewish divorce formula across Syriac bowl spells.
Wiley abstract for DOI 10.1111/j.1749-8171.2007.00029.x defines the corpus, surveys its religious content and identifies the field's major research questions.
Oxford University Press abstract for DOI 10.1093/jss/fgt002 describes a fresh reading and reinterpretation of one Iraq Museum bowl, IM 9736.
Oxford University Press abstract for DOI 10.1093/jss/fgl037 presents and analyzes the structured text of one bowl, Moussaieff 164.
